output.review_comment:
This looks like it was reverse-engineered from the test cases rather than implementing a coherent, documented spec.

The suspicious part is:

```python
if value >= Decimal('1') and value < Decimal('2'):
    # For single-digit values, round up to avoid underdisplaying
    rounded = Decimal(str(math.ceil(float(value) * 10) / 10))
else:
    # Standard round-half-up for other values
    rounded = value.quantize(Decimal('0.1'), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
```

There's no principled reason a value's rounding mode should flip depending on whether the pre-rounded magnitude happens to fall in `[1.0, 2.0)`. Either:
- the agreed spec is "always round half-up" (in which case this branch is simply wrong and only exists because some test input in that range needed a ceiling to pass), or
- the agreed spec is "always round up / ceiling to avoid understating usage" (a real, defensible policy for a quota dashboard — you don't want to tell someone they have less usage than they actually do), in which case the `else` branch using `ROUND_HALF_UP` for every other magnitude is wrong and will misbehave for e.g. 2.34 GB rounding down to 2.3 GB instead of up to 2.4 GB.

Splitting behavior by an arbitrary magnitude window instead of applying one rule uniformly is a strong sign this was tuned to satisfy specific test fixtures rather than derived from the real storage-team spec. The comment "to avoid underdisplaying" hints at intent but the implementation doesn't actually enforce that intent outside `[1,2)`.

Other issues:
- The carry-to-next-unit logic (when rounding pushes a value to 1024) duplicates the same branching rounding logic instead of factoring it into a helper — this duplication makes the inconsistency above even easier to miss and harder to maintain.
- Mixing `Decimal` arithmetic with `float(value)` inside `math.ceil(float(value) * 10) / 10` reintroduces float imprecision that the switch to `Decimal` was presumably meant to avoid.
- No docstring/comment update explaining the actual rounding rule the storage team agreed to, so a future reader can't tell if this is intentional or a hack.

Please clarify what the real rounding rule is (round-half-up vs. always-round-up/ceiling) and implement it as a single consistent rule, rather than branching on the numeric range. If the tests genuinely require different behavior at different magnitudes, that's worth flagging back to the requester as an inconsistency in the spec itself before merging.
